Basic definitions
• The mammalian body made up of many cells that
are differentiated to become tissues and
organs. They all come from one single large
cell called Zygote; which is formed by fusion
of male and female cells.
• Two types of cells are found in the body;
A- Somatic cell: other cells of the body, associated
with the tissue formation and regeneration, produced
through a process of cell division called Mitosis, and
has Diploid number of chromosomes (46).
B- Germ cell: gives rise to the Gametes (female cell
ovum and a male cell sperm), produced (Gametogenesis)
through a process of cell division called Meiosis.
Both cells are having half of chromosomes (23), or
Haploid, and are the only cells in the body has this.

body.text:
Capacitation of the sperm
• Newly ejaculated sperm cannot fertilize oocyte.
• Capacitation occurs in the uterus and oviducts - Involved the removal of
inhibiting factors derived from seminal plasma.
• The plasma membrane of epididymis sperm contained protein and
carbohydrate compliments of sperm surface molecule. -These molecules
become coated with seminal plasma protein that mask portions of plasma
membrane.
• These protein coating with some of the surface molecules are removed during
sperm journey in the female uterine tract, exposing portion of the molecules
that can bind to the Zona pellucida of the oocyte.
• It is a process (5-7 hours) that allow the acrosome reaction to occur so that
the sperm can penetrate the zona pellucida of the oocyte.
